title: From finite observation to all time.
prompt: For F(x) = x/2 on ℝ and fixed point 0, which argument proves Lyapunov stability?
hint: The definition needs every sufficiently close start and every nonnegative time.

options.text: Twelve plotted points stayed nearby, so every future point must do so.
For any ε > 0 choose δ = ε. If |x₀| < δ, then |Fⁿ(x₀)| = |x₀|/2ⁿ ≤ |x₀| < ε for every n ≥ 0.
Zero never moves, so every map that fixes zero is stable.

feedback.pass: The bound covers every n ≥ 0, not only the displayed sample. Its assumptions and quantifiers are explicit.
feedback.fail: A proof must cover all times and a neighborhood of starting states, not only the reference orbit.
